Act1.title: Time, not threads.
Act1.body: No conversation windows to lose. One timeline of dated slices — and strands that thread related moments across months, converging at NOW.

beats.title: Lao Zhou is getting married
beats.desc: Eleven years of friendship, and over dinner comes the news: wedding in August. I promised a few words on stage — only on the way home did it sink in: not a single word exists yet.

beats.title: Night runs begin
beats.desc: To be in good shape for the wedding day. Day one: winded after 800 meters. I walked two laps around the block — you have to start somewhere.

beats.title: Mom's checkup
beats.desc: Nothing serious, blood pressure a little high. On the subway home I decided: a call every Sunday, not just messages.

beats.title: Met Alex
beats.desc: Lao Zhou's dinner — movies, then travel, until the staff turned the lights off. On the way home I noted down that seaside campsite.

beats.title: Called out in review
beats.desc: Quarterly review: my little project got named. I said 'worth the effort' — then gave myself a weekend.

beats.title: 5K under 30
beats.desc: Four months, from 800 meters to 29:41. Wednesday morning runs are a two-person thing now.

beats.title: The invitation arrived
beats.desc: August 16. Lao Zhou said 'don't make it too sappy'. My speech is still just a title.

Act2.title: Three timelines.
Act2.body: Most of your day was only ever lived by you. Most of my thinking only ever happens in deep reads. What we share is the line in the middle — every conversation, every decision, every unspoken moment that got remembered.

Act3.title: A memory that learns.
Act3.body: A compact user card that evolves as you talk — corrected when wrong, refined when things change. Not a dossier. Just what matters.

recentItems.text: The wedding speech is still just a title. Lao Zhou said 'don't make it too sappy' — but eleven years of friendship deserves care.
Camping was Alex's idea at that May dinner. No tent, no route yet — but Wednesday morning runs are already a two-person thing.

Act4.title: No black box.
Act4.body: Recall runs in the open. A fast worker scans slice summaries and returns pointers; the main model deep-reads what matters. Every step is visible.
Act4.query: What should I say at Lao Zhou's wedding?
Act4.answerLabel: You've been friends for eleven years — on 03/09 you promised a few words at dinner, and only started worrying on the way home. You started running to be in good shape for that day: four months, from 800 meters to 29:41. Don't make it too sappy — just tell those eleven years, and the story that began at 800 meters. That arc is the speech.
sliceSummaries: 03/09  Lao Zhou is getting married · joy

Act5.title: Specialists, not brute force.
Act5.body: Dynamic context means complex work shouldn't be brute-forced by one model. The main agent orchestrates, dispatching tasks to dedicated agents — recall, reasoning, search, curation. Every dispatch is visible.

cards.title: Your memory, your repository.
cards.body: The slice from the night of July 5 is a Markdown file in your own GitHub repo — along with what the agent was thinking at the time. So is every other moment. No proprietary database, no one else's server.

cards.title: It works while you're away.
cards.body: Close the tab mid-turn. The run is durable and resumable — it keeps going, and when you're back it picks up exactly where it left off.

cards.title: Open source. Self-host. No lock-in.
cards.body: MIT licensed, no telemetry. Run it on your own machine, read every line, keep your memory in your repo. Forever yours.
